title: seccomp: allow socket(2) only for an allow-list of families
body:
The default profile allowed socket(2) for every address family except AF_VSOCK, so any family the profile does not know about, such as AF_ALG, passes seccomp and relies on the LSM or the kernel config to be refused. Docker blocks AF_ALG deliberately.

Replace the catch-all allow rules with one allow rule per family, using the same list as moby/profiles (allowedSocketDomains). Families that are not listed now fail with ENOSYS, the profile default. AF_VSOCK keeps its explicit EPERM rule, and AF_NETLINK keeps the NETLINK_AUDIT restriction that depends on CAP_AUDIT_WRITE.

The allow rules compare the full 64-bit argument, so a value with the upper 32 bits set does not match and is denied, and no mask is needed.

This also makes socket and socketpair agree on which families they accept.

On ABIs that use socketcall(2) the arguments cannot be filtered by seccomp, so these rules apply to the direct socket and socketpair syscalls only. That limitation already existed and is unchanged.

Tested with podman and the regenerated seccomp.json: socket(AF_ALG) returned EACCES with the previous profile (SELinux) and EAFNOSUPPORT with SELinux labelling disabled, so seccomp did not stop it. It now returns ENOSYS. AF_UNIX, AF_INET, AF_INET6 and AF_NETLINK still work, NETLINK_AUDIT still needs CAP_AUDIT_WRITE, and AF_VSOCK is still EPERM.

Add tests for the allow-list and the NETLINK_AUDIT rule, and regenerate seccomp.json.

comments.body:
> While I don't necessarily think limiting the socket families is bad it may put us in a bad spot in terms of backwards compatibility.
> 
> cc @giuseppe @mtrmac @mheon @podman-container-tools/podman-maintainers

It's not a breaking change.  Compared with the current profile (everything allowed except AF_VSOCK), the families that become blocked are:
  - AF_ALG.   Docker has blocked it since CopyFail.
  - Legacy families that the kernel has removed or is removing: AF_AX25, AF_NETROM, AF_ROSE, AF_ISDN, AF_CAIF, AF_APPLETALK, AF_ATMSVC, AF_IPX, AF_DECnet, AF_ECONET, AF_IRDA, AF_WANPIPE.
  - AF_UNSPEC and family numbers from AF_MAX up, which aren't real families.

> AF_ALG. Docker has blocked it since CopyFail.

Right, which still means it is a breaking change for podman users who do use this.

> Legacy families that the kernel has removed or is removing: AF_AX25, AF_NETROM, AF_ROSE, AF_ISDN, AF_CAIF, AF_APPLETALK, AF_ATMSVC, AF_IPX, AF_DECnet, AF_ECONET, AF_IRDA, AF_WANPIPE.

Which would still break someone who uses a new podman an an old kernel where they could still use one of these protocols in theory.

I am not claiming these are common but it IS a breaking change as it could break someone.

I have previously advocated for blocking `AF_ALG` and am still 100% in favor.

For the rest... Honestly, I don't think it'll be a problem. Appletalk kernel support was yanked this year, for example... I think most of the rest are in a similar place.

I am LGTM
